rows.title: Today: one PDF, one track, a page for every figure
rows.note:
Measured against the built page (DESIGN.md §5, §10):

• Adding: one PDF at a time. A .xml is refused (“This file isn’t a PDF.”). The 806 XBRL files on hand would take 806 picks.
• The ladder: four steps on one track. “Reading the statements” is the only working step, so numbers and text can’t be told apart, an hour of indexing has no step, and waiting_for_xbrl has no word.
• Many at once: the slip shows one file; Earlier gives every other file one word.
• The figure panel: From, On the page and “Open the PDF at page N” all need a page. An XBRL fact has an element and a context, no page, so three of its five lines would be empty.

The shared board on the right is the copy every direction uses: each pipeline state, each outcome of the PDF check, and what is said aloud.

rows.title: A · Two tracks on the slip
rows.note:
The bet: keep today’s page and change as little as works.

• The ladder keeps four numbered steps. Step 3, Reading, holds two tracks, Numbers above Text, each with a word and its counts. Whichever track is working is the ink block.
• Earlier becomes Your documents, with a Numbers and a Text column.
• A folder arrives as one sending line and one refusal summary. The slip asks for a company once for all its files (“Add Coastline Bank for all 26 files”).
• Figure panel: the same spec list, with From and Filed as for XBRL and In the PDF for the check. The button opens the results PDF at its statement pages, which classification already knows. No new backend read.

Cost: lowest. StageLadder gets a split third step and Earlier gets two columns. Asks: bulk company confirm, queue position (“2 ahead”).
Weak at 806: the list is 806 rows, newest first, and the slip shows only one company at a time.

rows.title: B · The work list
rows.note:
The bet: the batch is the unit. One ledger of every file, grouped by what it needs (Need you, Working, In line, Ready), counts at the top, and the slip beside the selected row.

• The slip’s ladder becomes a track table: a Numbers line and a Text line, a word per step.
• Need you lists companies, not files: one row per company with its codes and file count, and Add or It’s one of mine. The first is the screen’s one primary action.
• Figure panel: it opens with the sentence “Filed as XBRL data, not read off a page.” Below it, a How it was filed disclosure gives the element, period, unit and file. Drawn here with the check failed.

Cost: medium. A new page layout, counts by group from the API, and a filter. Asks: bulk confirm, grouped counts, queue position.
Weak: a PDF and its XBRL are two rows apart, so partial coverage still has nowhere to show.

rows.title: C · Filings, not files (recommended)
rows.note:
The bet: the investor thinks in filings (one company, one period), not files. A filing’s PDF and its XBRL sit in one row, under their company.

• Each filing has the two tracks. waiting_for_xbrl is visible as the PDF waiting on the XBRL beside it.
• Opened, a filing lists each statement’s source: profit and loss from XBRL, cash flow from the PDF by Gemini. This is spec §6.3’s slot rule made visible, so partial coverage has a home.
• The 806-file folder becomes “Not in your workspace yet”, one row per company with filing and file counts, confirmed once.
• Figure panel: From names the XBRL filed with the PDF, and In the PDF gives the page the check found the figure on. The button opens that page.

Cost: highest. The API groups by company and period, with sources per statement and the page of the match. Asks: all of the purple list.
Why recommended: it is the only direction where the 806-file needs-you edge and partial coverage both fall out of the structure instead of being bolted on.

rows.title: D · Two lines of work
rows.note:
The bet: say the machine’s day plainly. Numbers are quick and run two at a time; text is slow and runs one file at a time. The page leads with what each line is doing and who is next, then the documents.

• Text shows the one file being indexed: page 140 of 286, OCR pages, passages and the start time, with the ruler as the page’s one motion. Next is a numbered list, in arrival order.
• The phone slip has two short ladders, Numbers and Text, each with its own numbered steps. A partial index says which pages had no text.
• Figure panel: Every reading of this line. The XBRL value (Used) and the annual report’s Gemini reading (Not used: XBRL takes the year), with the PDF check underneath. Drawn with the check not run (no PDF).

Cost: medium. The queue order of index jobs (ask), and the panel needs every revision for the slot (ask).
Weak: the lanes describe the machine, not the investor’s filings, and with 806 files Next is long and mostly XBRL notes.

shared:
In every direction:

• The drop strip says “Drop PDFs or XBRL files here”, with Choose files and Choose a folder (dragging is never the only way). The limit, “PDF or XBRL (.xml), up to 50 MB a file”, is said before anything is chosen.
• A batch sends as one line, “Sending 214 of 806 files from bse-xbrl…”, with the ruler. Closing the tab asks first while files are still sending.
• Refusals are summarised once per batch, naming each file and why. Never a Notice per file.
• Each track says its state in words and counts: “Page 140 of 286”, never a percentage or a time left.
• An XBRL file’s text is “12 notes indexed. It has no pages.”, never “0 of 0 pages”.
• An unmapped XBRL format says so, and the PDF’s numbers are read instead.
• Screen readers hear batch milestones and each new question, nothing else.
• At most one primary action per screen, even with 31 companies waiting.
• The figure panel never shows a context id (OneD, FourD). The period comes from its dates, and the element name is a muted second line.
• Every outcome of the PDF check has words: found; not found (bold, and the figure stays as filed); and not checked for each reason (no PDF, a scan, no statement pages, the check turned off). See the shared board.
• The Research table’s note changes: “Each year comes whole from one filing: an XBRL filing first, otherwise the newest filing that prints it.”
• The research frames show 2025–26 from a Q4 XBRL. That assumes yes to the open Q4 question.
asks:
Backend asks (spec §11’s pipeline object doesn’t carry these):

1. Partial coverage. numbers.source is one value, but §6.3.2 lets a PDF take profit and loss from XBRL and cash flow from Gemini. Needs a source per statement (C2, C4).
2. Which XBRL a PDF waits on. numbers.state = waiting doesn’t name the document; covered_by_xbrl is only for not_needed (A1, C1, D1).
3. Unmapped format. XBRL_FORMAT_UNMAPPED is a revision warning with no pipeline word. Needs numbers.state or a reason (all).
4. Queue position for document.index (“2 ahead”, D’s Next list). Can come from queued jobs’ order.
5. Bulk company confirm: one confirm releases every held file printing the same ScripCode or ISIN (A2, B2, C2).
6. The page where xbrl_in_pdf found the value (C4’s “page 5”). Without it, the panel opens the statement pages (A3, B3).
7. Every revision for a slot, used and not used (D3).
8. Grouped counts by state for a batch (B’s count strip).
questions:
Open questions (one word each):

1. Q4 XBRL for annual years? The research frames assume yes, so 2025–26 is from the Q4 XBRL. If no, an XBRL figure shows only in the quarter view (data layer phase 4), and the panel waits for it.
2. Element names: always as a muted line (A, C), or only behind How it was filed (B)?
3. Confirm a company once for all its files (every direction draws it)? Or one file at a time, as today?

Pick a letter, mix them (“C with D’s readings panel”), or tell me what’s off.
